## STATISTICAL ANALYSIS - MelbourneFB_DW

\# Purpose: hypothesis tests and exploratory plots supporting BQ7 (weather), BQ2/BQ3 (trading hours), BQ1 (supply-demand).

\# Outputs are figures for the defence slides.

\# Principle: AGGREGATE IN SQL, ANALYSE IN R. \# Never pull 1.6M rows into the R session.

```{r}
library(DBI)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# 0. CONNECTION
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# If the driver name fails, run odbc::odbcListDrivers() to list installed ones.
con <- dbConnect(odbc::odbc(),
                 Driver   = "ODBC Driver 17 for SQL Server",
                 Server   = "LAPTOP-DBD3DPCV",
                 Database = "MelbourneFB_DW",
                 Trusted_Connection = "Yes")

dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM dw.DimBlock")
i64 <- sapply(hourly, function(x) inherits(x, "integer64"))
hourly[i64] <- lapply(hourly[i64], as.numeric) 
# expect 604
```

```{r}
# =====================================================================
# PART 1 -- HOURLY PANEL  (feeds BQ7, BQ2, BQ3)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# Grain: 1 day x 1 hour, pedestrians summed across stable-panel sensors.
#
# Only sensors with IsInStablePanel = 1 (~62 sensors, >= 95% hour coverage).
# Reason: mixing newly installed and decommissioned sensors makes the
# time series reflect HOW MANY SENSORS WERE ONLINE rather than actual
# foot traffic.
#
# Melbourne weather comes from a single station, so every sensor shares
# the same condition in a given hour -- aggregating to city level is valid.
#
# Expected size: ~17,520 rows.
# =====================================================================
sql_hourly <- "
SELECT
    d.FullDate,
    d.DayOfWeekNumber,
    d.DayName,
    d.IsWeekend,
    d.IsPublicHolidayVIC,
    d.SeasonName,
    t.TimeKey                AS Hour,
    t.Daypart,
    t.InCafeWindow,
    t.InLunchWindow,
    t.InAllDayWindow,
    t.InNightWindow,
    w.IsRaining,
    w.TemperatureBand,
    w.PrecipitationBand,
    AVG(CAST(f.TemperatureC AS FLOAT))      AS TempC,
    AVG(CAST(f.PrecipitationMM AS FLOAT))   AS PrecipMM,
    SUM(CAST(f.TotalPedestrians AS BIGINT)) AS Ped
FROM dw.FactFootfallHourly f
JOIN dw.DimDate    d ON d.DateKey    = f.DateKey
JOIN dw.DimTime    t ON t.TimeKey    = f.TimeKey
JOIN dw.DimWeather w ON w.WeatherKey = f.WeatherKey
JOIN dw.DimSensor  s ON s.SensorKey  = f.SensorKey
WHERE s.IsInStablePanel = 1
  AND f.SensorKey  <> -1
  AND f.WeatherKey <> -1
GROUP BY d.FullDate, d.DayOfWeekNumber, d.DayName, d.IsWeekend,
         d.IsPublicHolidayVIC, d.SeasonName,
         t.TimeKey, t.Daypart, t.InCafeWindow, t.InLunchWindow,
         t.InAllDayWindow, t.InNightWindow,
         w.IsRaining, w.TemperatureBand, w.PrecipitationBand
"
hourly <- dbGetQuery(con, sql_hourly)
i64 <- sapply(hourly, function(x) inherits(x, "integer64"))
hourly[i64] <- lapply(hourly[i64], as.numeric)

# NOTE ON BIT COLUMNS
# SQL Server BIT arrives in R as logical TRUE/FALSE, not 0/1.
# as.integer() normalises both cases: TRUE -> 1, and integers pass through.
# Without it, factor(x, levels = c(0,1)) silently produces all NA and
# lm() then fails with "contrasts can be applied only to factors with
# 2 or more levels".
hourly <- hourly %>%
  mutate(
    IsRaining = factor(as.integer(IsRaining), levels = c(0, 1),
                       labels = c("No rain", "Rain")),
    IsWeekend = factor(as.integer(IsWeekend), levels = c(0, 1),
                       labels = c("Weekday", "Weekend")),
    TemperatureBand   = factor(trimws(TemperatureBand),
                               levels = c("Cold", "Mild", "Warm", "Hot")),
    PrecipitationBand = factor(trimws(PrecipitationBand),
                               levels = c("None", "Light", "Heavy")),
    Hour = as.integer(Hour)
  )

# Sanity checks -- all must show every level with no NA
nrow(hourly)                  # expect ~17,500
table(hourly$IsRaining)       # rain typically 15-25% of hours
table(hourly$TemperatureBand)
summary(hourly$Ped)
```

```{r}
# =====================================================================
# PART 2 -- BQ2 / BQ3: SHAPE OF THE DAY
# =====================================================================

# 2a. 24-hour curve, weekday vs weekend.
#     This is the chart that drives the opening-hours recommendation.
p_profile <- hourly %>%
  group_by(Hour, IsWeekend) %>%
  summarise(MeanPed = mean(Ped), .groups = "drop") %>%
  ggplot(aes(Hour, MeanPed, colour = IsWeekend)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(size = 1.5) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 23, 3)) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("Weekday" = "#2E5C6E",
                                 "Weekend" = "#C08A2E")) +
  labs(title = "Pedestrian volume by hour of day",
       subtitle = "Mean across stable-panel sensors, Aug 2024 - Aug 2026",
       x = "Hour of day", y = "Mean pedestrians", colour = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)
print(p_profile)

# 2b. Does the peak hour differ between weekday and weekend?
hourly %>%
  group_by(IsWeekend, Hour) %>%
  summarise(MeanPed = mean(Ped), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(IsWeekend) %>%
  slice_max(MeanPed, n = 1)

# 2c. Share of traffic captured by each of the four trading windows.
#     The windows OVERLAP by design, so these sum to more than 100%.
#     If they sum to exactly 100% the BIT columns were built wrong.
hourly %>%
  summarise(
    Cafe   = sum(Ped[InCafeWindow   == 1]) / sum(Ped) * 100,
    Lunch  = sum(Ped[InLunchWindow  == 1]) / sum(Ped) * 100,
    AllDay = sum(Ped[InAllDayWindow == 1]) / sum(Ped) * 100,
    Night  = sum(Ped[InNightWindow  == 1]) / sum(Ped) * 100
  )

# 2d. BQ3: share of traffic after 22:00, split weekday/weekend.
#     Drives the "is late-night trade worth it" decision.
hourly %>%
  group_by(IsWeekend) %>%
  summarise(ShareAfter22h = sum(Ped[Hour >= 22]) / sum(Ped) * 100,
            .groups = "drop")

```

```{r}
# =====================================================================
# PART 3 -- BQ7: DOES RAIN REDUCE FOOT TRAFFIC?
# =====================================================================

# 3a. Raw comparison -- DO NOT put this number in the slides.
hourly %>%
  group_by(IsRaining) %>%
  summarise(Mean = mean(Ped), Median = median(Ped), n = n())

# Why it is unusable: rain is not randomly distributed. It concentrates
# in winter and in certain hours, so the raw gap confounds rain with
# season and time of day. The cross-tab below makes that visible.
table(hourly$SeasonName, hourly$IsRaining)

# 3b. Controlled estimate -- THIS is the number for the slides.
#     log1p because pedestrian counts are strongly right-skewed.
#     factor(Hour) absorbs the shape of the day, DayName the weekday
#     effect, TemperatureBand separates temperature from rain.
m <- lm(log1p(Ped) ~ factor(Hour) + DayName + TemperatureBand + IsRaining,
        data = hourly)

# Confirm the coefficient name before extracting it
rownames(summary(m)$coefficients)

rain_term  <- "IsRainingRain"
coef_rain  <- coef(m)[rain_term]
pct_change <- (exp(coef_rain) - 1) * 100
ci         <- (exp(confint(m)[rain_term, ]) - 1) * 100
p_value    <- summary(m)$coefficients[rain_term, "Pr(>|t|)"]

cat(sprintf(
  "Rain changes pedestrian volume by %.1f%% (95%% CI: %.1f%% to %.1f%%), p = %.4g\n",
  pct_change, ci[1], ci[2], p_value))

# 3c. Is heavy rain different from light rain?
#     Informs whether awnings / covered seating are worth the capital.
#     "None" is the reference level, so coefficients read as change
#     relative to dry conditions.
m2 <- lm(Ped ~ factor(Hour) + DayName + TemperatureBand + PrecipitationBand,
         data = hourly)
precip_rows <- grep("PrecipitationBand", rownames(summary(m2)$coefficients))
summary(m2)$coefficients[precip_rows, ]

# 3d. Rain effect broken out by hour.
#     If rain only bites at lunchtime, outdoor seating may still pay off.
p_rain <- hourly %>%
  group_by(Hour, IsRaining) %>%
  summarise(MeanPed = mean(Ped), .groups = "drop") %>%
  ggplot(aes(Hour, MeanPed, colour = IsRaining)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 23, 3)) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("No rain" = "#2E5C6E",
                                 "Rain"    = "#5B7F52")) +
  labs(title = "Rain effect by hour of day",
       x = "Hour of day", y = "Mean pedestrians", colour = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)
print(p_rain)
```

```{r}
# =====================================================================
# PART 4 -- BQ1: SUPPLY vs DEMAND BY BLOCK
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# Only 68 blocks have BOTH footfall coverage AND non-zero seating
# (see test T36 in 11_integrity_check.sql). This is the single largest
# limitation of the project and must be stated explicitly in the slides.
# =====================================================================
sql_block <- "
SELECT
    b.BlockID,
    b.AreaName,
    b.CLUESmallArea,
    b.DaytimePopulationBand,
    a.TotalSeats,
    a.TotalFBVenues,
    a.TotalJobs,
    ff.AvgDailyPed
FROM dw.FactBlockAnnual a
JOIN dw.DimBlock b ON b.BlockKey = a.BlockKey
JOIN (
    SELECT BlockKey,
           SUM(CAST(TotalPedestrians AS BIGINT)) * 1.0
             / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT DateKey), 0) AS AvgDailyPed
    FROM dw.FactFootfallHourly
    WHERE BlockKey <> -1
    GROUP BY BlockKey
) ff ON ff.BlockKey = a.BlockKey
WHERE a.IsLatestCensusYear = 1
  AND a.TotalSeats > 0
"
blocks <- dbGetQuery(con, sql_block) %>%
  mutate(SeatSaturation = TotalSeats / (AvgDailyPed / 1000))
i64 <- sapply(blocks, function(x) inherits(x, "integer64"))
blocks[i64] <- lapply(blocks[i64], as.numeric)
blocks <- blocks[blocks$AvgDailyPed >= 2000, ]
nrow(blocks)   


# 4a. Does supply follow demand?
#     Spearman, since the relationship need not be linear and n is small.
#     A weak correlation is the core argument for the whole project:
#     it means the market has NOT allocated seating efficiently.
cor.test(blocks$AvgDailyPed, blocks$TotalSeats, method = "spearman")

# 4b. Supply-demand scatter. Bottom-right quadrant = high demand,
#     low supply = the opportunity.
p_block <- ggplot(blocks, aes(AvgDailyPed, TotalSeats)) +
  geom_point(aes(size = TotalFBVenues), colour = "#2E5C6E", alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE, colour = "#C08A2E", fill = "#E8E4DC") +
  scale_size_continuous(range = c(2, 8)) +
  labs(title = "Seating supply against pedestrian demand",
       subtitle = paste0(nrow(blocks), " blocks with both data sources, 2024 census"),
       x = "Mean daily pedestrians", y = "Total F&B seats",
       size = "Venues") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)
print(p_block)
# 4d. Most saturated blocks -> the avoid list
blocks %>%
  arrange(desc(SeatSaturation)) %>%
  select(BlockID, AreaName, AvgDailyPed, TotalSeats, SeatSaturation) %>%
  head(10)

# 4e. Does saturation differ across CLUE small areas?
#     Kruskal-Wallis: no normality assumption, appropriate for small n.
#     With 68 blocks spread over many areas each group is tiny, so this
#     guards against reading a difference that is really just noise.
kruskal.test(SeatSaturation ~ factor(CLUESmallArea), data = blocks)

blocks %>%
  group_by(CLUESmallArea) %>%
  summarise(Blocks = n(),
            MedianSaturation = median(SeatSaturation),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(MedianSaturation)
```

```{r}
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. EXPORT FIGURES
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
ggsave("profile_24h.png",   p_profile, width = 8, height = 4.5, dpi = 150)
ggsave("rain_effect.png",   p_rain,    width = 8, height = 4.5, dpi = 150)
ggsave("supply_demand.png", p_block,   width = 8, height = 5.5, dpi = 150)

dbDisconnect(con)
```
